title: kelmo gate

macos.because: the seatbelt the runtime builds is macOS's: tests/test_runtime_macos.py asks a confined child for the network, a private file, a write to its code, a child process and a hard link, so a Mac run measures that file and every other host reports its section absent

interpreter.because: this suite is the locked environment pyproject.toml and uv.lock fix: run-tests.sh takes this folder's own .venv/bin/python when uv sync has built one and the PATH python3 otherwise (GATE_PYTHON overrides both), and an interpreter that carries none of the modules below measures none of the sections that need them, so the header says which interpreter measured the suite

src.because: tests/ import kelmo from src/, and test children start with cwd inside tests/, so PYTHONPATH has to carry the absolute path and not the name

pytest.because: the suite is run by pytest, which is in the dev group of pyproject.toml; the three CI-excluded lanes are unittest files pytest also collects

ruff.because: the lint the suite cannot replace: it saw an undefined json in a helper no test called, and it is a dev-group module of the same locked environment

fastmcp.because: src/kelmo/mcp.py builds the stdio server the MCP cases drive, and tests/test_mcp.py imports it

sqlite-vec.because: src/kelmo/store/db.py loads the vec0 extension when a case opens a database, so every case that stores or searches stops at the load

fastembed.because: src/kelmo/store/memory/embed.py builds the embedding model the vector cases rank with

networkx.because: the graph service and its navigation cases build the wiki graph through networkx

numpy.because: the embedding and vector-search cases carry numpy arrays through the store

python-frontmatter.because: the wiki compiler reads and writes page front-matter, and the wiki cases assert on it

markdown-it-py.because: the wiki compiler parses the page body with markdown-it before it builds the graph

pyyaml.because: the config and settings cases read YAML files, and the installer writes them

shellcheck.because: a gate that never lints its own folder re-accumulates what a sweep removes, and the installed launcher is shell a person types every day

bash32.because: the host is macOS bash 3.2 and Kelmo promises 3.2-compatible shell, so a launcher that only parses under bash 4 is broken there and not here

modeldir.because: docs/TARGET-STATE.md 1.4 requires a named directory holding the five pinned model files, and every frozen scenario starts by importing them into a vault; explicitly name it with KELMO_GATE_MODEL_DIR or KELMO_MODEL_DIR (the first set variable wins). No deployment path is assumed. The five-file probe still decides, so a directory of the right name holding other files stays a SKIP that says so

prefix.because: tests/test_installed_cli.py runs the launcher a pip-installed runtime ships, and the file defaults to .venv, which is a uv virtualenv whose bin/kelmo console script only reports E_RUNTIME; the lane runs when the launcher answers version, and is a SKIP that says so otherwise

bwrap.because: src/kelmo/linux_runtime.py:41-43 looks at exactly these two paths and raises IsolationError when it finds neither, so the failure names the tool and not the code

userns.because: bubblewrap builds its sandbox from an unprivileged user namespace, so the binary alone does not say whether installing it here would measure the Linux lane
userns.costs: whether installing bubblewrap on this host would measure the Linux kernel boundary at all: a host that refuses the unprivileged user namespace would only move the red from 'no bubblewrap' to 'cannot create a namespace'

sections.label: ruff check .

sections.label: the source suite

sections.skipped_leaves: the wheel and sdist artifact acceptance in tests/test_distribution.py, which skips itself unless KELMO_TEST_WHEEL and KELMO_TEST_SDIST name freshly built artifacts

sections.label: acceptance

sections.name: the lanes CI keeps out of the source suite (the runtime builder and the Linux kernel boundary)
sections.label: the excluded lanes

bound.reason: linux_runtime.execute() builds the sandbox through bubblewrap, which this gate asked for at both paths src/kelmo/linux_runtime.py looks at; the lane is measured on the Linux hosts the runtime is built for, and it is the only place this folder measures that another process's arguments are unreadable

sections.leaves: the runtime command builder and the Linux kernel boundary: unshare-all, NoNewPrivs, CapEff, the hidden host /proc/TARGET/environ, the hidden host /proc/TARGET/cmdline and the single /proc/net/route entry

sections.name: the installed CLI lane (the launcher over a pip-installed prefix)
sections.label: the installed CLI
sections.leaves: the installed runtime as a pip-installed prefix: the CLI and stdio MCP graph navigation a person gets after install.py, the wheel-vs-installed byte comparison, and the hiding path - `kelmo forget` through the installed launcher, read back through its own hybrid search, list, show, trace and status. The launcher bytes themselves are exercised in the source suite by tests/test_user_launcher.py

sections.name: the macOS kernel boundary (the seatbelt a confined child runs under)
sections.label: the macOS lane
sections.leaves: that a child confined by the runtime's seatbelt is denied TCP and UDP, the private canary's content and metadata, a write to its code, a child process and a hard link, while it can still write its scratch directory

unmeasured: the wheel and sdist build lanes docs/CI.md runs (the artifacts job and the four installed lanes): this gate never builds an artifact, so unless KELMO_TEST_WHEEL and KELMO_TEST_SDIST name freshly built ones the two parity cases in tests/test_distribution.py skip themselves and the gate names them under the suite section
the native launchd/systemd service lifecycle, clean-machine bootstrap and real Claude/Codex provider acceptance stay separate from these checks, as docs/CI.md says

CI collects none of the three lane files sections 6 and 8 run through unittest (tests/test_runtime.py, tests/test_linux_runtime.py, tests/test_runtime_macos.py): its source job ignores them, so this gate alone measures them, and a pytest-only fixture added to them would run nowhere

whether a confined macOS runtime hides another process's arguments is measured nowhere: the seatbelt policy macos_policy() builds does not deny the same-UID KERN_PROCARGS2 read (a Mac run of this folder read SYNTHETIC_ONLY=test-value out of another process's arguments), docs/RUNTIME-SECURITY.md keeps that same-UID gap open and calls native macOS an unverified host-credential boundary, and the claim that process arguments are unreadable belongs to the Linux adapter and is measured only by tests/test_linux_runtime.py::test_kernel_boundary, which is BOUND wherever the host refuses unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)
